studies.Reference: Diet in the epidemiology of bladder cancer in western New York.
studies.Title: Diet in the epidemiology of bladder cancer in western New York.
studies.Authors: Vena JE, Graham S, Freudenheim J, Marshall J, Zielezny M, Swanson M, Sufrin G
studies.Population: White male residents of Erie, Niagara, and Monroe counties of western New York
studies.comparison_type: Cases versus controls for dietary vitamin D intake (no quantitative estimate reported)

sample_size.excerpt: We present the dietary epidemiology of bladder cancer while controlling for a number of lifestyle and environmental risk factors in a study of 351 white male cases with histologically confirmed transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder and 855 white male controls selected from Erie, Niagara, and Monroe counties of western New York from 1979 to 1985.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 351 + 855 = 1206

cases.excerpt: We present the dietary epidemiology of bladder cancer while controlling for a number of lifestyle and environmental risk factors in a study of 351 white male cases with histologically confirmed transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder and 855 white male controls selected from Erie, Niagara, and Monroe counties of western New York from 1979 to 1985.

comparison.excerpt: No significant differences between cases and controls were seen for intake of calcium, retinol, thiamin, riboflavin, niacin, vitamin C, vitamin D, and vitamin E.

design.excerpt: in a study of 351 white male cases with histologically confirmed transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder and 855 white male controls

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Usual diet was estimated by comprehensive interviews with use of a detailed food frequency questionnaire.

studies.Reference: Plasma 25-hydroxyvitamin D(3) and bladder cancer risk according to tumor stage and FGFR3 status: a mechanism-based epidemiological study.
studies.Title: Plasma 25-hydroxyvitamin D(3) and bladder cancer risk according to tumor stage and FGFR3 status: a mechanism-based epidemiological study.
studies.Authors: Amaral AF, Méndez-Pertuz M, Muñoz A, Silverman DT, Allory Y, Kogevinas M, Lloreta J, Rothman N, Carrato A, Rivas del Fresno M, Real FX, Malats N, Spanish Bladder Cancer/EPICURO Study investigators
studies.Journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute
studies.Population: urothelial bladder cancer cases and control subjects
studies.comparison_type: lowest versus highest plasma 25(OH)D3 concentration category

sample_size.excerpt: Plasma concentrations of 25(OH)D(3) in 1125 cases with UBC and 1028 control subjects were determined by a chemiluminescence immunoassay.
sample_size.location: abstract, methods; total_n derived from reported group counts 1125 + 1028 = 2153

cases.excerpt: Plasma concentrations of 25(OH)D(3) in 1125 cases with UBC and 1028 control subjects were determined by a chemiluminescence immunoassay.

effect_size.excerpt: A statistically significantly increased risk of UBC was observed among subjects presenting the lowest concentrations of 25(OH)D(3) (OR(adj) = 1.83; 95% CI = 1.19 to 2.82; P = .006), showing a dose-response effect (P (trend) = .004).

confidence_interval.excerpt: A statistically significantly increased risk of UBC was observed among subjects presenting the lowest concentrations of 25(OH)D(3) (OR(adj) = 1.83; 95% CI = 1.19 to 2.82; P = .006), showing a dose-response effect (P (trend) = .004).

studies.Reference: Bladder Cancer is Associated with Low Plasma 25-hydroxyvitamin D Concentrations in Tunisian Population.
studies.Title: Bladder Cancer is Associated with Low Plasma 25-hydroxyvitamin D Concentrations in Tunisian Population.
studies.Authors: Ben Fradj MK, Gargouri MM, Hammami MB, Ben Rhouma S, Kallel A, Jemaa R, Feki M, Nouira Y, Kaabachi N
studies.Population: Tunisian patients with urothelial bladder cancer and healthy controls
studies.Smoking Status: Mixed (adjusted for smoking status and duration of smoking)
studies.comparison_type: Vitamin D deficiency (25-OHD <30 nmol/L) versus sufficient concentrations

sample_size.excerpt: A case-control study included 250 patients with UBC and 250 healthy controls.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 250 + 250 = 500

cases.excerpt: A case-control study included 250 patients with UBC and 250 healthy controls.

effect_size.excerpt: Multivariate analysis showed that UBC is associated with vitamin D deficiency [odd-ratio (95% confidence interval), 3.71 (1.76-7.80); P = 0.001] and vitamin D insufficiency [2.65 (1.40-5.01); P = 0.003].

confidence_interval.excerpt: Multivariate analysis showed that UBC is associated with vitamin D deficiency [odd-ratio (95% confidence interval), 3.71 (1.76-7.80); P = 0.001] and vitamin D insufficiency [2.65 (1.40-5.01); P = 0.003].

comparison.excerpt: Vitamin D deficiency and insufficiency were defined as 25-OHD <30 nmol/L and 30 to 49.99 nmol/L, respectively.

design.excerpt: A case-control study included 250 patients with UBC and 250 healthy controls.

continent.excerpt: Bladder Cancer is Associated with Low Plasma 25-hydroxyvitamin D Concentrations in Tunisian Population

ethnicity.excerpt: urothelial bladder cancer (UBC) risk in Tunisians

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Plasma 25-OHD was assessed by a competitive chemiluminescence immunoassay.
